title: The Chicago-to-Memphis excursion: pay and playing in the baggage car
summary: His made-up band was paid $15 a man, he cleared $305, and they played in a baggage car with beer and gambling.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Whose band was that? Your one?

Mine. Little made up band. Let me tell you what happened. I asked Francois who had the band. He wouldn't come, you know. None of them didn't want to come. So I got me a little made up band. And when we come, the boy, Charlie Allen, that was the man running. He asked them, did they want a wedding partnership or did they want a salary? No, man, no partnership. Let's give us $15 a man. Dick, they had a great big yard, see. And they pay at the gate. Down the quarter at the gate. And that yard was packed and jammed. The hall was packed and jammed. You couldn't get any, see. So he paid them the $15. Took them the five of them. And I worked with it. You see, I worked with it. And they paid all them orders. And they said, what you ready to give me, Dick?

$305. Boy, I never made that much money before in my life. And did you know they got mad with me? And he asked them how did they want to wait. Asked them in front. Now that wasn't my fault, was it? No.
Well, people are jealous, you know.
That's right. They just figured we wasn't going to make nothing. And boy, I never seen so many people.
What did you do on the excursion?

Well, to take that baggage car, see. They got barrels of beer on the side. And they got gambling over there. And they got the space. You know, got them two doors barred off, you know, bars keep you from falling out. And we sat way up in the corner with the band. Them people danced like hell out there. And you got so many hours to play. You get so much for them hours and you come back, play so many more hours. We played from time to two to three o'clock in the morning. Just train running and we playing. Yeah. Yeah. That must have been good. That was good, Dick. All that stuff was good, partner. What kind of gambling games did they play? Huh? What kind of card games? They played poker. Mm-hm.
